newsitem.title: USA: Omnicom Group to buy Fleishman-Hillard.
newsitem.headline: Omnicom Group to buy Fleishman-Hillard.

text.p: Advertising powerhouse Omnicom Group Inc. said Wednesday it agreed to buy public relations firm Fleishman-Hillard Inc. for an undisclosed amount of cash and stock.
New York-based Omnicon said it signed a letter of intent to buy the employee-owned company, which is based in St. Louis.

Omnicom said the transaction would create the largest global public relations group, which would include Fleishman-Hillard and its Porter Novelli International unit. Combined sales would reach about $300 million in 1997, Omnicom said.
Sources familiar with the pending transaction valued the deal at between $85 million and $100 million.
John Graham, chairman of Fleishman-Hillard, also will serve as chairman of the new group and report to John Wren, president and chief executive officer of Omnicom.
Robert Druckenmiller, president and CEO of Porter Novelli, will become president of the newly formed group.
Ketchum Public Relations Worldwide, which was purchased by Omnicom in 1996, will operate as a separate agency outside the group.
Omnicom Group, a communications and advertising company, includes the ad agencies BBDO Worldwide; DDB Needham Worldwide and TBWA Chiat/Day.
